summary.text: Karen Engleman, a Republican from Georgetown, has served in the Indiana House of Representatives since 2016 and represents House District 70, which includes Harrison County and portions of Clark, Floyd and Washington counties.
She is the assistant majority floor leader and chairs the Statutory Committee on Ethics.

paragraphs.text: Before her election to the legislature in 2016, Engleman served three terms as Harrison County Auditor and spent seven years as Crandall Town Clerk-Treasurer.
Her caucus biography says she attended Corydon Central High School, Indiana University Southeast, Bellarmine University and Jefferson Community College.

In 2018, Governing Magazine honored her as a Public Official of the Year for her work on sexual harassment prevention, and she authored a law requiring at least one hour of annual sexual harassment training for all members of the Indiana General Assembly.
She also sits on the Government and Regulatory Reform and Local Government committees.
She and her husband, Gary, have five children and 10 grandchildren, and she is a member of Oak Grove United Methodist Church and the Corydon Rotary Club.
